synthesizedFacts.fact: Keratosis pilaris is a common, harmless skin condition characterized by small, painless bumps on the skin, often on the upper arms, thighs, cheeks, or buttocks.
The condition is caused by the buildup of keratin, which blocks the opening of hair follicles.
Keratosis pilaris is more common in children and teenagers and often improves with age, typically disappearing by age 30.
Treatment is not necessary, but moisturizers and exfoliating creams can improve the appearance of the skin.
Keratosis pilaris is often associated with other skin conditions such as eczema and ichthyosis vulgaris.
